scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page.purpose: The main matching workspace of a bank reconciliation: book transactions (checks, deposits, transfers, JEs to cash) on one side, bank transactions on the other, with running totals showing the difference still to be explained.
scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page.outcome: Every book and bank item for the period is either matched, carried as an outstanding item, or booked as a new transaction, until the difference is zero.
scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page.rootCause: Reconciliation is fundamentally a matching exercise between two independent records of the same cash. A dedicated workspace with live difference totals shows exactly how far the preparer is from a true balance.
scr_cash_reconcile_bank_account_page.ifSkipped: Preparers match in spreadsheets, lose track of what was matched, and finish with an unexplained difference.
redFlags: Difference cleared with a manual adjustment rather than matched items

scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.purpose: Filters and sorts book and bank transactions on the reconciliation page — by type, amount, date or check number — to find matches quickly in accounts with thousands of resident ACH receipts.
scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.outcome: Preparers find matching pairs fast and isolate the handful of genuinely unmatched items.
scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.rootCause: Large multifamily operating accounts can have thousands of transactions a month. Without filtering by amount or type, finding the one unmatched $1,250 NSF return is impractical.
scr_cash_filtering_and_sorting_transacti.ifSkipped: Reconciliations take hours longer and unmatched items are missed.
redFlags: Reconciliations completed without reviewing unmatched items by type

scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.purpose: Matches book and bank transactions by hand when auto-matching cannot — for example a single bank deposit covering several book deposits, or checks with keying differences.
scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.outcome: Items the system could not pair automatically are matched with preparer judgment.
scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.rootCause: Banks batch and split transactions differently from the books (a remote-deposit capture may combine several days of deposits). Manual matching resolves these many-to-one cases.
scr_cash_reconciling_an_account_manually.ifSkipped: Legitimate items remain unmatched and are carried forward as false reconciling items.
redFlags: Manual matches where amounts differ

scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.purpose: Allows matching a group of different transaction types (e.g., a deposit and a reversal, or a check and its void) together when their net amount is zero, clearing offsetting items with no bank impact.
scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.outcome: Offsetting book entries that never reached the bank are cleared together.
scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.rootCause: A check issued and voided in the same period, or a deposit reversed and re-entered, produces pairs that net to zero and never appear at the bank. They must be cleared together or they sit as outstanding forever.
scr_cash_matching_different_transaction_.ifSkipped: Offsetting pairs remain as permanent outstanding items, inflating the outstanding list.
redFlags: Zero-net matches of unrelated transactions

scr_cash_matching_a_range_of_checks_quic.purpose: Quick Match clears a whole range of check numbers at once when the bank statement shows them all cleared at their issued amounts.
scr_cash_matching_a_range_of_checks_quic.outcome: High-volume check clearing is done in seconds instead of check by check.
scr_cash_matching_a_range_of_checks_quic.rootCause: Properties paying many vendors by check can have hundreds clearing each month. Range matching saves time but must only be used when amounts agree, since an altered check would be hidden.
scr_cash_matching_a_range_of_checks_quic.ifSkipped: Check clearing is slow; misused, it can hide a fraudulently altered check amount.
gaap: UCC 4-406 — duty to examine statements for alterations
redFlags: Quick match used when bank and book amounts differ

scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction.purpose: Undoes a match made in error on the reconciliation page so the items can be matched correctly.
scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction.outcome: Mistaken matches are corrected before the reconciliation is finalized.
scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction.rootCause: Auto-matching and quick-matching can pair the wrong items with the same amount. Unmatching is the correction path before the reconciliation is locked.
scr_cash_unmatching_a_transaction.ifSkipped: Wrong matches stay, hiding a real unmatched item.
redFlags: Frequent unmatch/rematch activity on the same items

scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.purpose: Exports the reconciliation's matched and unmatched transactions to Excel for analysis, reviewer questions or attachment to the close package.
scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.outcome: A portable copy of reconciliation detail for review and support.
scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.rootCause: Reviewers and auditors often ask for detail of outstanding items or unusual matches in Excel, and offshore teams use it to investigate aged items with site staff.
scr_cash_exporting_bank_reconciliation_t.ifSkipped: Reviewers cannot easily analyze reconciling items and follow-up with site teams is slower.
redFlags: Exports edited and presented as system output

scr_cash_excluding_bank_transactions.purpose: Excludes bank transactions that are not relevant to the reconciliation — for example duplicate lines in an imported bank file or memo-only lines.
scr_cash_excluding_bank_transactions.outcome: Noise is removed from the bank side so real items stand out.
scr_cash_excluding_bank_transactions.rootCause: Bank files sometimes contain informational or duplicate entries. Excluding them prevents false unmatched items, but exclusion of real items would hide activity, so it needs care.
scr_cash_excluding_bank_transactions.ifSkipped: False unmatched items clutter the rec; if misused, real bank activity is hidden.
redFlags: Excluded items with real amounts (fees, returns)

scr_cash_marking_bank_transactions_as_re.purpose: Marks a bank transaction as a reconciling item to be resolved later — for example an unidentified deposit awaiting research or a bank error the bank has agreed to correct.
scr_cash_marking_bank_transactions_as_re.outcome: The reconciliation can be finalized with the item explicitly listed and tracked rather than forced.
scr_cash_marking_bank_transactions_as_re.rootCause: Some items cannot be resolved by the close deadline. Tracking them as reconciling items makes them visible and aged instead of being plugged.
scr_cash_marking_bank_transactions_as_re.ifSkipped: Unresolved items are plugged or forgotten.
redFlags: Reconciling items older than 60 days

scr_cash_viewing_alternate_bank_accounts.purpose: Views transactions in alternate bank accounts during a reconciliation — helpful when an item was recorded to the wrong account (e.g., a deposit booked to operating that actually went to the trust account).
scr_cash_viewing_alternate_bank_accounts.outcome: Mis-posted items between accounts are identified and corrected.
scr_cash_viewing_alternate_bank_accounts.rootCause: Transactions posted to the wrong bank account create offsetting unmatched items in two recs. Seeing the other account reveals the pair.
scr_cash_viewing_alternate_bank_accounts.ifSkipped: Two recs carry offsetting items for months.
redFlags: Recurring items posted to the wrong account

scr_cash_finalizing_the_reconciliation.purpose: Completes the reconciliation once all appropriate items are matched and the remaining difference is zero, locking the matched items and producing the reconciliation record.
scr_cash_finalizing_the_reconciliation.outcome: A finalized reconciliation that becomes part of the close evidence.
scr_cash_finalizing_the_reconciliation.rootCause: Finalizing freezes the result so later changes cannot silently alter it. It marks the point at which the preparer asserts the account is reconciled.
scr_cash_finalizing_the_reconciliation.ifSkipped: Reconciliations remain open and can be changed after review.
redFlags: Finalized reconciliations with a non-zero difference

scr_cash_editing_or_voiding_reconciled_t.purpose: Explains how edits or voids of transactions already reconciled affect the reconciliation — typically requiring the reconciliation to be reopened or the change dated in the current period.
scr_cash_editing_or_voiding_reconciled_t.outcome: Changes to reconciled items are made without silently breaking prior reconciliations.
scr_cash_editing_or_voiding_reconciled_t.rootCause: Voiding a check that already cleared, or editing a reconciled deposit, changes a closed reconciliation's balance. The rules exist to force such changes into the current period.
scr_cash_editing_or_voiding_reconciled_t.ifSkipped: Prior reconciliations break, and next month's beginning balance no longer agrees.
redFlags: Voids dated into reconciled periods

scr_cash_troubleshooting_reconciliation.purpose: Guidance for resolving reconciliation differences before finalizing — checking the statement ending balance, beginning balance, duplicate matches, transactions dated outside the period and unrecorded bank items.
scr_cash_troubleshooting_reconciliation.outcome: The preparer finds the true cause of a difference instead of forcing a balance.
scr_cash_troubleshooting_reconciliation.rootCause: Common causes of differences are predictable (wrong ending balance, changed prior rec, missed bank fee). A checklist gets preparers to the cause quickly.
scr_cash_troubleshooting_reconciliation.ifSkipped: Differences are plugged and real errors or fraud remain hidden.
redFlags: Round-dollar adjustments to force balance

scr_cash_credit_card_reconciliation.purpose: Reconciles company credit card accounts to issuer statements — recorded charges, fees and payments versus the statement — with setup required the first time.
scr_cash_credit_card_reconciliation.outcome: Card liability balances agree with issuer statements monthly.
scr_cash_credit_card_reconciliation.rootCause: Credit cards are an unapproved-spend risk; reconciling them monthly confirms every charge was recorded, coded and paid.
scr_cash_credit_card_reconciliation.ifSkipped: Unrecorded or personal charges go unnoticed and the card liability is misstated.
redFlags: Card reconciliations not performed monthly

scr_cash_setting_up_an_account_for_recon.purpose: First-time setup of a credit card account for reconciliation — opening balance and outstanding charges at the start date.
scr_cash_setting_up_an_account_for_recon.outcome: Card reconciliations start from a correct opening position.
scr_cash_setting_up_an_account_for_recon.rootCause: Like bank recs, card recs need a verified opening balance; otherwise every later month carries the initial error.
scr_cash_setting_up_an_account_for_recon.ifSkipped: Card reconciliations start with an unexplained difference.
redFlags: Opening balance not matching the issuer statement

scr_cash_reconciling_credit_cards.purpose: Monthly card reconciliation — entering the statement balance and matching recorded charges, fees and payments to the statement.
scr_cash_reconciling_credit_cards.outcome: Every card charge on the statement is recorded, coded and matched.
scr_cash_reconciling_credit_cards.rootCause: Card charges are often recorded late or not at all by site staff; the reconciliation is where missing charges surface.
scr_cash_reconciling_credit_cards.ifSkipped: Missing charges are discovered only when the issuer demands payment.
redFlags: Statement charges without recorded transactions

scr_cash_bank_feeds_list.purpose: Lists bank feed transactions imported automatically from banks (via subscription) for all accounts, ready for matching in reconciliations.
scr_cash_bank_feeds_list.outcome: Daily bank activity is available in RealPage without manual file downloads.
scr_cash_bank_feeds_list.rootCause: Daily bank feeds allow continuous reconciliation and early detection of unauthorized transactions, instead of waiting for month-end statements.
scr_cash_bank_feeds_list.ifSkipped: Unauthorized debits are discovered weeks later at month-end.
gaap: UCC 4-406 — timely review of bank activity
NACHA — 60-day window for unauthorized ACH returns
redFlags: Unmatched feed transactions older than a week

scr_cash_configuring_the_bank_feeds_list.purpose: Enables the bank feeds subscription and configures which accounts receive feeds.
scr_cash_configuring_the_bank_feeds_list.outcome: Bank feeds flow for the accounts that need daily monitoring.
scr_cash_configuring_the_bank_feeds_list.rootCause: Bank feeds require a subscription and account-level setup; without it, the team relies on manual statement downloads.
scr_cash_configuring_the_bank_feeds_list.ifSkipped: Manual statement downloads and slower detection of problems.
redFlags: Active bank accounts without feeds configured

scr_cash_deleting_an_unmatched_transacti.purpose: Deletes an unmatched bank feed transaction — for example a duplicate feed line — from the bank feeds list.
scr_cash_deleting_an_unmatched_transacti.outcome: Duplicate feed lines no longer appear as unmatched items.
scr_cash_deleting_an_unmatched_transacti.rootCause: Feeds occasionally duplicate transactions; deleting duplicates keeps the rec accurate. Deleting real transactions would hide bank activity, so this needs care.
scr_cash_deleting_an_unmatched_transacti.ifSkipped: Duplicate feed lines inflate unmatched items; misuse hides real debits.
redFlags: Deleted feed transactions that appear on the bank statement

scr_cash_bulk_bank_feed_import_page.purpose: Imports bank transaction files for many accounts at once — a consolidated CSV or BAI2 file from the bank covering every property account.
scr_cash_bulk_bank_feed_import_page.outcome: Portfolio-wide bank activity loaded in one step for reconciliation.
scr_cash_bulk_bank_feed_import_page.rootCause: Banks commonly provide one consolidated file for all accounts of a management company. Importing it at once is far faster than per-account imports.
scr_cash_bulk_bank_feed_import_page.ifSkipped: Accountants download and import files per account, delaying recs.
redFlags: Accounts in the file not mapped to RealPage bank accounts

scr_cash_importing_a_consolidated_csv_or.purpose: Imports one consolidated CSV or BAI file that contains transactions for all bank accounts, mapping each to its RealPage bank account.
scr_cash_importing_a_consolidated_csv_or.outcome: All accounts receive their bank transactions from a single upload.
scr_cash_importing_a_consolidated_csv_or.rootCause: Consolidated bank files are standard in treasury services; mapping them correctly is necessary so transactions land in the right account's reconciliation.
scr_cash_importing_a_consolidated_csv_or.ifSkipped: Transactions land in the wrong account or are skipped.
redFlags: Unmapped account numbers skipped silently

scr_cash_importing_a_csv_or_bai_file_for.purpose: Imports a CSV or BAI file for one bank account, used when the bank provides account-level files or a single account needs reloading.
scr_cash_importing_a_csv_or_bai_file_for.outcome: One account's bank activity loaded for reconciliation.
scr_cash_importing_a_csv_or_bai_file_for.rootCause: Smaller banks often provide only per-account files; single-account imports cover these cases.
scr_cash_importing_a_csv_or_bai_file_for.ifSkipped: The account's activity must be keyed manually.
redFlags: File date range overlapping a prior import

scr_cash_editing_or_deleting_a_layout_fo.purpose: Maintains the column layout that tells RealPage how to read a bank's consolidated CSV file (which column is account, date, amount, description).
scr_cash_editing_or_deleting_a_layout_fo.outcome: Bank files are parsed correctly after a bank changes its format.
scr_cash_editing_or_deleting_a_layout_fo.rootCause: Banks change file formats without notice; an outdated layout misreads amounts or dates and loads wrong data.
scr_cash_editing_or_deleting_a_layout_fo.ifSkipped: Imports fail or load wrong amounts after a bank format change.
redFlags: Import totals not matching bank totals after a layout change

scr_cash_reconciling_items_list.purpose: Lists all transactions marked as reconciling items across accounts, with age, so they can be followed up and resolved.
scr_cash_reconciling_items_list.outcome: A portfolio-wide list of open reconciling items with aging for escalation.
scr_cash_reconciling_items_list.rootCause: Reconciling items that are not tracked centrally get carried forward indefinitely. Aging them forces resolution — and items over 90 days are an audit finding.
scr_cash_reconciling_items_list.ifSkipped: Old reconciling items accumulate and hide errors or fraud.
redFlags: Items older than 90 days

scr_cash_bulk_reconciliation_page.purpose: Manages bulk reconciliation — automatically matching and reconciling many bank accounts at once using bank feeds and matching rules.
scr_cash_bulk_reconciliation_page.outcome: Most accounts reconcile automatically, leaving only exceptions for manual work.
scr_cash_bulk_reconciliation_page.rootCause: Large portfolios have hundreds of accounts. Bulk reconciliation lets a small team keep up by handling only exceptions.
scr_cash_bulk_reconciliation_page.ifSkipped: Each account must be reconciled manually, delaying the close.
gaap: COSO 2013 — automated controls with exception review
redFlags: Auto-reconciled accounts never reviewed

scr_cash_starting_a_bulk_reconciliation_.purpose: Starts a bulk reconciliation run immediately rather than waiting for the schedule — for example after a late bank file arrives.
scr_cash_starting_a_bulk_reconciliation_.outcome: Accounts are reconciled as soon as data is available.
scr_cash_starting_a_bulk_reconciliation_.rootCause: Close deadlines do not wait for schedules; on-demand runs keep recs moving when files arrive late.
scr_cash_starting_a_bulk_reconciliation_.ifSkipped: Recs wait for the next scheduled run, losing a day of the close.
redFlags: On-demand runs started before all bank files were imported

scr_cash_manually_reconciling_bank_accou.purpose: Manually reconciles multiple accounts at once from the bulk page when the system has matched everything but needs the preparer to confirm.
scr_cash_manually_reconciling_bank_accou.outcome: Fully matched accounts are finalized in one step.
scr_cash_manually_reconciling_bank_accou.rootCause: Confirmation by a preparer is still required for accountability even when matching is automatic; doing it in bulk keeps it efficient.
scr_cash_manually_reconciling_bank_accou.ifSkipped: Fully matched accounts remain pending and delay the close.
redFlags: Bulk confirmation of accounts with reconciling items

scr_cash_pending_bank_reconciliations_li.purpose: Lists bank reconciliations that have been started but not finalized, by account and statement period, so the team can see which accounts are still open for the close.
scr_cash_pending_bank_reconciliations_li.outcome: Clear visibility of which bank accounts are not yet reconciled for the period.
scr_cash_pending_bank_reconciliations_li.rootCause: Close status depends on every account being reconciled by the deadline (typically business day 3-5). The pending list shows exactly which are still open, including ones abandoned mid-way.
scr_cash_pending_bank_reconciliations_li.ifSkipped: Half-finished recs are forgotten and the property's close package goes out missing bank reconciliations.
redFlags: Reconciliations pending from prior months

scr_cash_viewing_and_finalizing_open_ban.purpose: Opens pending reconciliations from the pending list to review the remaining items and finalize them once the difference is zero.
scr_cash_viewing_and_finalizing_open_ban.outcome: Nearly-complete recs are closed out quickly and moved to approval.
scr_cash_viewing_and_finalizing_open_ban.rootCause: Many pending recs need only a last check before finalizing. Working them from the pending list is the fastest way to clear the backlog before the close deadline.
scr_cash_viewing_and_finalizing_open_ban.ifSkipped: Recs remain open, never reach the approver, and the close checklist shows cash as incomplete.
redFlags: Recs finalized without reviewing reconciling items

scr_cash_generating_a_pending_bank_recon.purpose: Produces a report of all pending (unfinalized) bank reconciliations by account, preparer and age, for monitoring and escalation during close.
scr_cash_generating_a_pending_bank_recon.outcome: Managers can escalate specific late reconciliations before the owner reporting deadline.
scr_cash_generating_a_pending_bank_recon.rootCause: Onshore managers need a portable status report of open recs to chase preparers and to explain delays to clients.
scr_cash_generating_a_pending_bank_recon.ifSkipped: Late recs are not escalated in time and owner packages go out without complete bank reconciliations.
redFlags: The same accounts pending month after month

scr_cash_reconciliation_histories_list.purpose: Lists completed reconciliations per account with statement dates, balances and status, and gives access to reconciliation reports, attached statements and reopening.
scr_cash_reconciliation_histories_list.outcome: A complete history of every account's reconciliations for audit and reference.
scr_cash_reconciliation_histories_list.rootCause: Auditors, lenders and owners request prior reconciliations, and gaps in monthly history are an immediate finding. The history also shows whether any reconciliation was reopened after approval.
scr_cash_reconciliation_histories_list.ifSkipped: Prior reconciliations cannot be produced on request and gaps in history go unnoticed until an audit.
redFlags: Gaps in monthly reconciliation history

scr_cash_reopening_and_adjusting_a_close.purpose: Reopens a finalized reconciliation to correct it — for example when an item was matched to the wrong bank line or a transaction in the period was later voided.
scr_cash_reopening_and_adjusting_a_close.outcome: Errors in closed reconciliations are corrected with a record that the rec was reopened and why.
scr_cash_reopening_and_adjusting_a_close.rootCause: Mistakes are sometimes found after finalizing. A controlled reopen path fixes them, but every reopening changes evidence that may already have been reviewed, so it needs justification and re-approval.
scr_cash_reopening_and_adjusting_a_close.ifSkipped: Errors carry forward into every later month, or reconciliations are changed after approval without anyone re-reviewing them.
gaap: COSO 2013 — change controls over completed controls
redFlags: Reopened recs after approval without re-approval

scr_cash_attaching_a_bank_statement_to_a.purpose: Attaches the bank statement PDF for the period to the reconciliation record, so the reviewer can confirm the ending balance used in the rec against the bank's own document.
scr_cash_attaching_a_bank_statement_to_a.outcome: Each reconciliation carries its external evidence, ready for review and audit.
scr_cash_attaching_a_bank_statement_to_a.rootCause: The ending bank balance is the anchor of the reconciliation. Reviewers and auditors rely on the bank's statement, not a keyed number, to verify it.
scr_cash_attaching_a_bank_statement_to_a.ifSkipped: Reviewers approve recs without seeing the statement, or must request it separately, delaying approval.
redFlags: Recs approved without an attached statement

scr_cash_generating_a_reconciliation_rep.purpose: Produces the reconciliation report — bank balance, outstanding checks, deposits in transit, adjustments and book balance — for a finalized reconciliation.
scr_cash_generating_a_reconciliation_rep.outcome: The formal reconciliation document for the close package.
scr_cash_generating_a_reconciliation_rep.rootCause: The report is the standard evidence of the bank reconciliation control that owners, lenders and auditors expect.
scr_cash_generating_a_reconciliation_rep.ifSkipped: No formal evidence of the reconciliation.
redFlags: Reports generated before finalization

scr_cash_generating_an_outstanding_items.purpose: Lists outstanding checks, deposits in transit and reconciling items as of a reconciliation date.
scr_cash_generating_an_outstanding_items.outcome: A schedule of items that explain the difference between bank and book, with ages.
scr_cash_generating_an_outstanding_items.rootCause: Outstanding items must be aged and reviewed; stale checks move to escheatment and old deposits in transit indicate problems.
scr_cash_generating_an_outstanding_items.ifSkipped: Stale items are not identified for follow-up or escheatment.
redFlags: Outstanding checks older than 180 days

scr_cash_generating_an_adjusted_items_re.purpose: Lists adjustments made during a reconciliation — transactions or JEs created for bank-only items.
scr_cash_generating_an_adjusted_items_re.outcome: Reviewers see every entry the preparer booked to make the rec balance.
scr_cash_generating_an_adjusted_items_re.rootCause: Adjustments made during reconciliation are the highest-risk items (potential plugs); a separate report focuses review on them.
scr_cash_generating_an_adjusted_items_re.ifSkipped: Plugs and improper adjustments escape review.
redFlags: Adjustments to miscellaneous or suspense accounts

scr_cash_generating_a_package_with_multi.purpose: Produces one package combining multiple bank reconciliations — for a property with several accounts or for a portfolio — for the close package or owner request.
scr_cash_generating_a_package_with_multi.outcome: All of a property's bank recs delivered as one document.
scr_cash_generating_a_package_with_multi.rootCause: Owners and auditors typically want every account's reconciliation for a period; a combined package saves assembling them manually.
scr_cash_generating_a_package_with_multi.ifSkipped: Packages are assembled by hand and accounts get left out.
redFlags: Packages missing trust or reserve accounts

scr_cash_approve_bank_reconciliations_li.purpose: Lists bank reconciliations submitted for approval, where the approver reviews each one and approves or declines it.
scr_cash_approve_bank_reconciliations_li.outcome: An approval queue that documents independent review of every bank reconciliation.
scr_cash_approve_bank_reconciliations_li.rootCause: Independent review of bank recs is one of the key controls auditors test. The queue is where that review happens and is evidenced with a name and timestamp.
scr_cash_approve_bank_reconciliations_li.ifSkipped: Reconciliations are prepared but never independently reviewed, and the control fails audit testing.
redFlags: Recs pending approval past the close deadline

scr_cash_approving_and_declining_bank_re.purpose: Approver's action to approve a reconciliation or decline it with comments for correction.
scr_cash_approving_and_declining_bank_re.outcome: Approved recs are locked as close evidence; declined ones return to the preparer.
scr_cash_approving_and_declining_bank_re.rootCause: Approval documents that someone independent examined the reconciling items; declines evidence that the review found problems.
scr_cash_approving_and_declining_bank_re.ifSkipped: No evidence of review; problems are not sent back for correction.
redFlags: Approvals without comments on aged reconciling items

scr_cash_opting_out_of_approval_notifica.purpose: Lets users stop receiving email notifications for bank reconciliation approvals.
scr_cash_opting_out_of_approval_notifica.rootCause: High-volume approvers may receive hundreds of emails at close, but opting out risks missing items they must approve, so it should be used with care.
scr_cash_opting_out_of_approval_notifica.ifSkipped: Notification fatigue; if misused, approvers miss pending recs.
redFlags: Approvers opted out with pending items aging in their queue

scr_cash_sample_email_notifications_for_.purpose: Shows examples of the email notifications sent during bank reconciliation approval (submitted, approved, declined).
scr_cash_sample_email_notifications_for_.outcome: Users recognize legitimate approval emails and know what action each requires.
scr_cash_sample_email_notifications_for_.rootCause: Knowing the genuine notification format helps staff act on real requests and recognize phishing emails that imitate system notifications.
scr_cash_sample_email_notifications_for_.ifSkipped: Staff miss or misread approval requests, or fall for imitation emails.
redFlags: Notification emails asking users to enter credentials

scr_cash_debit_cards_for_petty_cash.purpose: Explains prepaid debit cards issued to site staff in place of physical petty cash, with spending tracked by expense category and reimbursed through an approval workflow.
scr_cash_debit_cards_for_petty_cash.outcome: Small site purchases are made with traceable cards rather than cash boxes.
scr_cash_debit_cards_for_petty_cash.rootCause: Physical petty cash at leasing offices is a common source of shortages and misappropriation. Prepaid cards give transaction-level visibility and limit exposure to the loaded balance.
scr_cash_debit_cards_for_petty_cash.ifSkipped: Cash boxes continue with little traceability and frequent unexplained shortages.
redFlags: Card spend without receipts or categories

scr_cash_configuring_debit_cards_for_pet.purpose: Configures the petty cash debit card program — expense categories, funding bank accounts and reimbursement settings.
scr_cash_configuring_debit_cards_for_pet.outcome: Card spending maps to GL expense accounts and reimbursements draw from the right bank account.
scr_cash_configuring_debit_cards_for_pet.rootCause: Without configured categories and funding, card spending cannot be coded or replenished correctly.
scr_cash_configuring_debit_cards_for_pet.ifSkipped: Card spending is uncoded and reimbursements post incorrectly.
redFlags: Categories mapped to capital accounts

scr_cash_enabling_debit_cards_for_petty_.purpose: Turns on petty cash debit cards and defines expense categories (e.g., office supplies, resident events, minor repairs) that staff choose when spending.
scr_cash_enabling_debit_cards_for_petty_.outcome: Staff can use cards with spending categorized for GL coding.
scr_cash_enabling_debit_cards_for_petty_.rootCause: Categories drive coding of card spend to the right expense accounts for budget reporting.
scr_cash_enabling_debit_cards_for_petty_.ifSkipped: Card spend lands in a single miscellaneous account.
redFlags: Too few categories to support budget reporting

scr_cash_enabling_bank_accounts_for_pett.purpose: Enables the specific property operating bank accounts that fund replenishment of petty cash debit cards, so reloads draw from the property whose staff spent the money.
scr_cash_enabling_bank_accounts_for_pett.outcome: Card replenishments come from the correct property's operating account.
scr_cash_enabling_bank_accounts_for_pett.rootCause: Replenishing from the wrong account charges one owner's cash for another property's spending. Trust or reserve accounts must never be used for this.
scr_cash_enabling_bank_accounts_for_pett.ifSkipped: Replenishments fail, or they draw from the wrong property's or a restricted account.
redFlags: Security deposit trust accounts enabled for petty cash replenishment

scr_cash_setting_up_permissions_for_pett.purpose: Sets which users can issue cards, load funds, view transactions and approve reimbursements.
scr_cash_setting_up_permissions_for_pett.outcome: Segregated duties across card issuance, spending and reimbursement approval.
scr_cash_setting_up_permissions_for_pett.rootCause: If the same person issues, spends and approves reimbursement, card programs become a fraud channel.
scr_cash_setting_up_permissions_for_pett.ifSkipped: One person controls the whole card cycle.
redFlags: Cardholders who can approve their own reimbursements

scr_cash_configuring_approvals_for_petty.purpose: Configures an approval workflow so petty cash card reimbursements require approval before funds are loaded.
scr_cash_configuring_approvals_for_petty.outcome: Card replenishments are reviewed before more money is loaded.
scr_cash_configuring_approvals_for_petty.rootCause: Approval before replenishment is the key control: it forces review of what was spent before more funds are made available.
scr_cash_configuring_approvals_for_petty.ifSkipped: Cards are reloaded automatically without review of prior spending.
redFlags: Reimbursements approved by the cardholder

scr_cash_issue_card_page.purpose: Page for issuing prepaid petty cash debit cards to authorized site staff or properties, setting limits and categories.
scr_cash_issue_card_page.outcome: Cards issued with defined limits to named holders.
scr_cash_issue_card_page.rootCause: Issuing cards to named individuals with limits creates accountability and caps exposure.
scr_cash_issue_card_page.ifSkipped: Cards shared among staff with no accountability.
redFlags: Cards issued to properties rather than named individuals without controls

scr_cash_issuing_a_pc_card.purpose: Procedure for issuing a petty cash card to a property and cardholder, with initial funding.
scr_cash_issuing_a_pc_card.outcome: A funded card ready for site purchases.
scr_cash_issuing_a_pc_card.rootCause: Initial funding must be recorded as a transfer to petty cash so the card balance is tracked in the GL.
scr_cash_issuing_a_pc_card.ifSkipped: Card funding is recorded as expense, overstating expenses.
redFlags: Card funding expensed at issue
